note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, hour, price and schedule below comes from the City of Boulder's own pages: the Racket Sports page for the outdoor court table and the reservation rules, the pickleball page for the indoor and outdoor drop-in schedules, the Racket Sports FAQs for the fee history, and each location's own page for the address, the hours and the amenities. Where the City is silent, on surface, on lighting and on when the courts are busy, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
Boulder answers parking at four of its five venues. The pages for the North Boulder, East Boulder and South Boulder recreation centres each carry the word "Parking" answered "Yes" under an ADA Accessibility heading. That is the whole statement: no lot size, no fee, no time limit.

Chautauqua Park is the exception. Its page is headed "Paid Parking in effect Memorial weekend to Labor Day", with paid parking "on summer weekends and holidays at Chautauqua and nearby neighborhood streets", and a Park-to-Park service that "provides free satellite parking and shuttle service". Foothills Community Park publishes nothing about parking. Restrooms are stated at all five venues.
slots.peak_hours:
The City does not say when its courts are busy. Outdoors, South Boulder sets aside "8:30 to 11:30 am on 6 outdoor courts" every day, and North Boulder "7:30 to 10:30 am on 4 outdoor courts" on Tuesdays and Thursdays plus "6 to 9 pm on 4 outdoor courts" on Wednesdays and Fridays. East Boulder, Chautauqua and Foothills have no scheduled session.

Outside those windows the courts are first come, or reservable at $10 an hour up to 7.5 days ahead, two hours a day at most, with no refunds for weather. Foothills is different again: its four courts exist from 7 a.m. to noon daily, and after noon the rink goes back to inline hockey.
slots.surface_condition:
The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Boulder. It names what they are drawn on: "Pickleball play is on tennis courts with pickleball lines", says the Racket Sports page, "Except for Foothills Community Park which is a designated inline hockey rink." The nine indoor courts are basketball gymnasium floors at drop-in times only, because "pickleball nets are not available outside listed drop-in hours".

The nets column of the table reads "Rolling" on every row. At Foothills there are none to roll: "Please bring your own portable pickleball nets. Nets are not available onsite."

When this was read South Boulder's eight outdoor courts were closed for "court resurfacing and restriping" from August 17, with a reopening the City called tentative. Lighting is not stated for any venue.
slots.local_scene:
Every one of Boulder's five published venues is free to play, on the City's own sentence, "Courts are first come and free to all park visitors, a reserved court is available to secure your date and time". Boulder is the first Colorado city on this site. It is one of seven cities on this site with a free court, and, with Cape Coral, one of only two where every published venue is free. It is also one of the few operators on this site that publishes a written drop-in schedule for both its indoor and its outdoor courts.

The City runs classes, lessons and a seasonal adult league at its three recreation centres. Reservation fees doubled from $5 to $10 an hour on November 14, 2025, the first increase since 2012. Tom Watson Park appears on the Racket Sports page only under "Additional Tennis Courts" with the figure 4, a tennis count, so no pickleball number is published for it.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts in one place
best_for.text: South Boulder Recreation Center has eleven courts, the largest set in Boulder: eight outdoor on the tennis courts with pickleball lines, and three indoor in the gymnasium on Sunday mornings and Tuesday and Thursday afternoons outside June to October. The City runs outdoor drop-in here every day, 8:30 to 11:30 am on six courts. The outdoor courts were closed for resurfacing when read, tentatively reopening September 11.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to play after work
best_for.text: North Boulder Recreation Center is the one venue where the City schedules an evening session outdoors: Wednesdays and Fridays, 6 to 9 pm, on four courts, plus Tuesday and Thursday mornings. Three indoor courts run Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings with the daily entry fee or a pass. The City places complimentary light timers near Tennis Court 1 here, while stating that lights are not guaranteed after sunset.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the longest published hours
best_for.text: Chautauqua Park is open 5:00 am to 11:00 pm daily, the longest stated hours of any Boulder venue, with two pickleball courts on a single tennis court, a game rather than a rotation. It is free and first come; reservations cost $10 an hour. The City states paid parking at and near the park on summer weekends and holidays, with a free satellite lot and shuttle through Park-to-Park.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Boulder have?
faqs.a: Twenty-nine across five City venues: eleven at South Boulder Recreation Center, seven at North Boulder Recreation Center, five at East Boulder Community Center, four at Foothills Community Park and two at Chautauqua Park. Twenty are outdoor, from the City's Racket Sports table, and nine are indoor, from the pickleball page's drop-in lines.

At the drop-in times the City prints for each gymnasium: Monday, Wednesday and Friday 7:30 to 10:30 am at North Boulder; Monday 1 to 3 pm and 6 to 8 pm and Sunday 2 to 4 pm at East Boulder; Sunday 9 to 11 am and Tuesday and Thursday 1:30 to 3:30 pm at South Boulder, with none there from June through October.
